differences.title: 1. Architecture
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB uses a shared-nothing architecture with shared memory for inter-thread communication, optimizing local node performance for time-series workloads.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse employs a columnar, shared-nothing architecture, excellent for analytical queries by reading only necessary columns, minimizing I/O.

differences.title: 2. SQL Dialect
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB offers a PostgreSQL-compatible SQL interface, easing migration and adoption for developers familiar with relational databases.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse supports ANSI SQL with extensive proprietary extensions for analytical functions, offering specialized query capabilities.

differences.title: 3. Indexing Strategy
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB utilizes a sparse primary index on timestamp and designated columns, enabling rapid range scans and lookups for time-series data.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse builds sparse indexes on columns (often the first in table definition), allowing efficient filtering on those specific fields.

differences.title: 4. Data Ingestion
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB is optimized for high-frequency, low-latency writes, ideal for real-time data streams and IoT scenarios.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse excels at batch inserts, efficiently processing large volumes of data at once for analytical purposes.

differences.title: 5. Query Performance
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB's indexing and memory-centric design accelerate time-series range queries and point lookups significantly.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse's columnar storage and vectorization provide exceptional performance for complex analytical aggregations over large datasets.

differences.title: 6. Data Storage
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB prioritizes memory for hot data, leveraging memory-mapped files for efficient disk access when needed.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse stores data in columnar files on disk, optimized for compression and sequential reads during analytics.

differences.title: 7. Use Cases
differences.leftDesc: QuestDB is well-suited for operational dashboards, real-time monitoring, and applications requiring low-latency time-series data access.
differences.rightDesc: ClickHouse shines in business intelligence, large-scale data warehousing, and complex ad-hoc analytical querying.
